title: Tilt-slide a quick-acting knob down a stud, square it on the washer, and turn it until its own thread clamps it snug
instruction: Tilt and slide the quick acting knob down the stud, square it on the washer, and turn it until it is snug.
context: AI hardware reliability technicians clamp GPU and edge-compute modules to vibration shaker plates with crossbars and quick-acting knobs (Carr Lane CLM-8-QAK). Pushed straight down, the knob jams on the top threads; it is tilted to slide down, squared so its half-threads catch, then turned until snug.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left, z up; table top z 74.75). Subplate (fixed): aluminum T-slot plate, 16 x 20 x 1.2 cm, at x 26, y 0, carrying a dark-anodized edge compute enclosure (9.0 x 10.3 x 3.5 cm) with silver heatsink stripes and a green PCB edge strip. Crossbar (fixed): 6061 aluminum, 2.5 x 18.0 x 1.2 cm, spanning y -9 to +9 cm over the module (top face z 80.65) on 3.5 cm spacer sleeves at y +7.5 and -7.5. The left stud (y +7.5) is clamped by a hex nut; the open right M8x1.25 steel stud at x 26, y -7.5 rises 5.5 cm above the crossbar to z 86.15 (5.0 mm core, 8.0 mm thread crests). Washer (free): zinc DIN 6340 M8 washer (8.4 mm bore, 23 mm OD, 4 mm thick) lying flat on the crossbar round the open stud. Staging block (fixed): blue anodized block, 4.4 x 4.4 x 1.2 cm, at x 20, y -15, with an 18 mm OD x 1.0 cm pedestal and a 4.2 mm, 0.8 cm tall brass peg. Knob (free): Carr Lane CLM-8-QAK quick-acting four-prong knob, sintered iron, 38 mm across the prongs, 17 mm hub, 22 mm tall, 41 g, relieved bore with two opposing half-thread lugs, prongs along x and y, a gold index mark on its -x prong, upright on the peg (center x 20, y -15, z 78.05).
scoring: Score 0.0 if the knob falls off the table (center below z 69.75 cm for 0.15 s) or jams: upright (tilt <= 5 deg), axis within 15 mm of the stud, touching its top threads (collider gap <= 0.3 mm, bottom within the top 8 mm of the stud) and not moving down, for 0.5 s; hovering or tilting clear of the stud is never penalized. Otherwise, at the end: 0.25 if the knob is on the stud (axis within 6 mm) with its bottom at least 3 cm down it; 0.5 if it is squared on the washer (knob face within 0.6 mm of the washer, axis within 4 mm, tilt <= 3 deg) for at least 1 s; 0.75 if, while squared, coaxial within 1.5 mm and its half-threads engaged on the stud thread, the knob was turned clockwise until its face met the washer (within 0.25 mm) and on at least 15 deg past that contact; 1.0 if also both grippers are 3 cm clear and the knob is still (< 2 mm/s) for the last 1.5 s. Turning a tilted, loose, off-axis or unengaged knob earns nothing.
fidelity: Approximate. Stud crests are discrete 8 mm collars and the knob's half-threads are two lugs: a 13 deg tilt clears them by 0.5 mm and an upright push stops on the top crest. The thread is a kinematic screw (1.25 mm lead, right hand) on the stud's first crest, reached only by the squared knob's own lug; it catches a quarter turn before face contact. Tightness is turns past face contact; the torque rise is a modelled friction, not a clamp force.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (both arms moved toward the block, knob stayed on the staging block); demo: 1 (right arm lifted the knob off the block, worked it onto the stud, then backed away)
